An `if` that checks the type of a value and then throws is saying "this value has the wrong type". `TypeError` is the built-in error for that, and the caller can tell it apart from other failures with `instanceof`.

The rule reports `throw new Error()` when it's the only statement inside the braces of an `if` or its `else`, and the condition is made of type checks: `typeof`, `instanceof`, `isNaN()`, `isFinite()`, or a method such as `Array.isArray()`, `Number.isInteger()` or `_.isString()`.

`--fix` changes `Error` to `TypeError`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"unicorn/prefer-type-error" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
function repeat(text, times) {
  if (typeof text !== "string") {
    throw new Error("text must be a string");
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(times)) {
    throw new Error("times must be an integer");
  }
  return text.repeat(times);
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function repeat(text, times) {
  if (typeof text !== "string") {
    throw new TypeError("text must be a string");
  }
  if (times < 0) {
    throw new Error("times must not be negative");
  }
  return text.repeat(times);
}
```
